Durham's Solar Energy Systems Ordinance, adopted by the Town Council on 2023-02-06 and codified in Zoning Ordinance Chapter 175 (section 175-53 Table of Uses and section 175-109.N), treats utility-scale solar as a principal use. It bars freestanding large utility-scale systems (over 100 kW and under 5 MW) from every district except two where a conditional use permit is needed. It bars freestanding small utility-scale systems from all residential and commercial core districts, bars freestanding systems from the Wetland and Shoreland overlays, and caps freestanding systems at 25 ft.
restrictions.long_description: zoning restriction: Large Utility-Scale solar (over 100 kW, under 5 MW) freestanding is X (prohibited) in R, RA, RB, RC, CB1, CB2, PO, CH, C, CC, OR and DBP, CU in MUDOR and ORLI; Small Utility-Scale solar (100 kW or less) freestanding is X in R, RA, RB, RC, CB1, CB2, PO, CH, C and CC, P in OR, MUDOR, ORLI and DBP; Large Group Net Metering Host freestanding has the same pattern as Large Utility-Scale; overlay_zone: freestanding solar energy systems prohibited in the Wetland Conservation Overlay District (175-62) and the Shoreland Protection Overlay District (175-73.M); height limit: freestanding systems 25 ft, up to 35 ft by special exception only in R, RC, OR, MUDOR, ORLI and DBP (175-109.N.9.c); front setback 100 ft for utility-scale (175-109.N.6.b, a road setback, not counted)

restrictions.description: Moultonborough Zoning Ordinance Article 10.2 (Solar Facilities Ordinance) sorts ground-mounted solar into use classes by acreage and capacity and, in its Table of Permitted Solar Uses, prohibits the larger classes in several districts. It caps any Solar Power Generation Station (over 30 MW) at 150 acres and requires every system to meet district building setbacks from lot lines.
restrictions.long_description: zoning restriction: Community, Accessory Agricultural, Primary Agricultural, Large Commercial, Industrial and Utility Solar and Solar Power Generation Stations are marked X (prohibited) in the Village Commercial C and Village Overlay districts; Industrial, Utility and Generation Station uses prohibited in West Village Overlay; Solar Power Generation Station prohibited in Commercial A and Commercial B (CUP only in Residential Agricultural); Commercial and larger uses need a Conditional Use Permit; cap on area: a Solar Power Generation Station shall in no case exceed 150 acres; setback: entire system, including panels, must meet district building setbacks from lot lines (tracking systems measured at closest approach)

restrictions.description: Town of Canaan approved an ordinance for large wind energy systems with specific height, setback, and shadow flicker requirements.
restrictions.long_description: In March 2018, the Town of Canaan in Granon County approved an ordinance for large wind energy systems that sets a maximum turbine blade diameter height of 350 feet, establishes a setback requirement of three times the turbine blade diameter height, and mandates that shadow flicker cannot exceed eight hours per year in total. The ordinance includes other requirements.

projects.description: In December 2016, the New Hampshire Site Evaluation Committee approved the 29-MW Antrim wind farm, which would involve 9 wind turbines on a ridge.
projects.long_description: In December 2016, the New Hampshire Site Evaluation Committee approved the 29-MW Antrim wind farm, which would involve 9 wind turbines on a ridge. Project opponents concerned about noise and impacts on wildlife, property values, and scenic views appealed the decision to the New Hampshire Supreme Court. In May 2018, the court ruled against the project opponents on all counts, allowing the project to move forward. The project began commercial operations in 2019.

projects.description: In April 2024, the New Hampshire Supreme Court overturned the City of Franklin Planning Board’s denial of a 6-acre, 1-MW solar farm proposed by GSSG New Hampshire.
projects.long_description: In April 2024, the New Hampshire Supreme Court overturned the City of Franklin Planning Board’s denial of a 6-acre, 1-MW solar farm proposed by GSSG New Hampshire. The project met the city’s zoning ordinances but was opposed by residents were concerned about disruptions of the scenery and property values. The court stated that a board cannot deny projects that comply with zoning ordinances based solely on subjective views. The court essentially approved the project by issuing a builder’s remedy which allows a project to proceed if it meets zoning ordinances.

projects.long_description: In 2010, a 99-MW, 33-turbine wind farm near Groveton was proposed. The Appalachian Mountain Club raised concerns that the project might impact sensitive high-elevation forest. However, the project was ultimately completed as originally planned in 2012.

projects.description: In 2018, NextEra Energy’s plans for a 10-MW, 54-acre solar farm in Concord were rejected by the local zoning board because there would be too much “impervious surface” for a residential open-space zoning lot.
projects.long_description: In 2018, NextEra Energy’s plans for a 10-MW, 54-acre solar farm in Concord were rejected by the local zoning board because there would be too much “impervious surface” for a residential open-space zoning lot. The zoning board denied the developer’s request for rehearing.

projects.description: The proposed 75.9-MW, 23-turbine Wild Meadows Wind Farm was abandoned in 2014.
projects.long_description: The proposed 75.9-MW, 23-turbine Wild Meadows Wind Farm was abandoned in 2014. In a statement the developer blamed “the current political and regulatory climate in New Hampshire.” The project faced opposition from residents and local groups including the Appalachian Mountain Club.
